title: Alkynes and the Triple Bond Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A welding torch, a miner's lamp that runs on a stone and water, and mangoes that ripen too fast all hide one gas: ethyne. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 9, Hydrocarbons) we learn alkynes: hydrocarbons with one carbon carbon triple bond.

On the molecule bench, two sp carbons build one sigma and two pi bonds into a linear triple bond (120 pm, 823 kJ/mol), a base pulls the acidic end hydrogen off with curved arrows, ethyne is made from calcium carbide and from a vicinal dihalide, propyne reacts with sodium and adds two HBr by Markovnikov's rule, and three ethyne molecules join into benzene at 873 K. Then the exam trap, an original JEE/NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 94 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Three puzzles, one gas
0:32 What is an alkyne
1:02 The molecule bench: building the triple bond
1:58 Why the end hydrogen is acidic
2:20 Pause and think: whose hydrogen leaves
2:36 Making ethyne, link by link
3:20 Worked example: propyne with Na and HBr
3:57 More additions and the benzene ring
4:26 Exam trap: but-2-yne and sodium
4:47 Practice question (JEE/NEET pattern)
5:23 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Benzene and Aromaticity. Why is benzene not like three double bonds?
